summary: The note is a local news feature on the Senior Art Exhibit "Celebrating Life and Creativity," held September 3–17, 2023 at the Downtown Community Arts Center. It presents interviews with the lead organizer, two senior artists, two visitors and a council member. The common theme is that creativity has no age limit and that art programs give seniors purpose and connect generations.
one_line: Local news feature on the Senior Art Exhibit "Celebrating Life and Creativity," featuring interviews with organizers, senior artists, visitors and a council member.
key_facts: The Senior Art Exhibit, titled "Celebrating Life and Creativity," runs from September 3rd to September 17th, 2023 at the Downtown Community Arts Center.
Lead organizer Jane Ellington says the exhibit is the culmination of over a year's worth of planning.
Jane Ellington says there are over sixty participants, and the response from local seniors has been overwhelming.
Edward "Ted" Johnson, a retired architect, paints watercolor landscapes and says watercolors let him capture the essence of a place without confinement.
Marta Sanchez has been sculpting in clay for the better part of two decades, and her sculptures represent chapters of her life as a mother, a worker and a grandmother.
Marta Sanchez's central message is one of evolution: people are always adapting and learning, no matter their age.
Charles Bennett, a young professional in his thirties, was impressed by the variety and quality of the art and said it felt raw and real compared with mainstream galleries.
Charles Bennett was admiring a detailed oil painting of a serene lakeside.
Seventeen-year-old high school student Lily Turner praised a vibrant mixed media piece as loud and exciting, not what she assumed senior art would be like.

Council member Tom Harding, an advocate for arts and culture, says the exhibit reinforces inclusivity and highlights the value of art programs for seniors, offering mental stimulation and a sense of purpose.
Ted Johnson said that architecture was about rigid lines and precise measurements, and that retirement led him to seek something more free.
The article was written as a first-person feature that includes interviews conducted on the exhibit's opening day.
